_comment: A metric monitor. Sentry calls it a detector of type metric_issue: it
watches a number and raises an issue when the number crosses a line.
It tells nobody by itself - rules/waitlist-submit-failed.json is the
workflow that does, and binds here by detectorName. That is why this
file carries no workflow_ids: the binding lives in rules/, as it does
for every other detector, and apply.sh refuses a file that carries it.
Why this monitor exists: nothing else catches a broken waitlist. A
submit that fails is handled - onSubmitFailed counts it and reports the
error - so the form still renders, no page 500s, and the issue alerts
stay quiet. The only visible symptom is that signups stop, which nobody
notices because signups are rare enough that zero looks like a slow
week.
THE AGGREGATE NAMES THE METRIC, AND THE QUERY IS EMPTY. The retired
../alerts/ file used count(value) with 'metric.name:waitlist.
submit_failed' in the query, which Sentry accepted and which matched
nothing. A trace metric is addressed inside the aggregate as
sum(value,<name>,<type>,<unit>). Same mistake the dashboard made and
fixed (onlooker-txcu.13); the shape below was read off a monitor built
by hand in the UI on 2026-09-26.
queryType 1 pairs with events_analytics_platform in Sentry's own
examples (0 goes with the errors dataset). The read shape of a detector
does not return it, so the API reference is the only evidence there is.
STATIC, NOT DYNAMIC. Anomaly detection learns seasonality from history,
and this metric has fired twice ever, both forced. Any failure at all
is the signal: above 0 opens a high-priority issue (75), 0 resolves it.
The name is how apply.sh finds this detector again, so renaming it in
Sentry means renaming it here and in the rule, or the next run creates
a second one.

detector.name: Waitlist submit failing (production)
detector.description: A waitlist signup failed. The form still renders, so this is the only sign that signups have stopped.
